repo_prior_art.cite: none; the closest active two-wave endpoint-minimax and bounded-cluster orbit-game proposals address different finite-population design problems

published_prior_art.cite: Janson2015 supplies the zero-long-run-variance/coboundary substrate; Leung2022ANI and FanLengWu2025 study one-wave asymptotic variance inference, not this finite-sample cross-wave Palm-covariance diagnostic
Leung2022ANI establishes one-wave network-HAC inference and interprets its finite-population bias, but does not give the stated repeated-wave finite-sample test
Janson2015 classifies the algebraic degenerate boundary but contains no statistical experiment or minimax separation theorem

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Two-wave diagnostic theorems
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The observable cross-wave moment requires two conditionally independent, washout-separated Bernoulli assignment waves on the same graph, exposure map, and no-carryover potential-outcome schedule.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The concentration and testing claims are conditional on that repeated-experiment design.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Proposition janson-boundary-corollary
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The coboundary characterization and endpoint law are imported from Janson2015 rather than claimed as new.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The null’s coboundary interpretation is conditional on Janson2015; the cross-wave identification and concentration claims are separate proposed contributions.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv preprint, 2013; corroborating version for the cited 2015 Journal of Applied Probability article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: For a stationary finite-variance m-dependent sequence, zero long-run variance is equivalent to a stationary (m-1)-dependent coboundary representation, and unnormalized centered sums have an endpoint-difference law.

The paper proves exposure-IPW consistency and approximate normality under ANI and studies a network-HAC variance estimator whose finite-population bias is interpretable as unit-level exposure-effect variance.
The paper gives a randomization-based interference framework using a design, exposure mapping, estimands, inverse-probability weighting, and randomization-based variance estimators.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:1109.0838; corroborating version for the cited SPA article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies stationary fields represented as measurable functions of iid innovations under short-range dependence, proving a CLT, invariance principle, and sample-autocovariance limit theorem.

source_verification_receipts.version: prepublication manuscript corresponding to Annals of Applied Probability 15(1A), 2005
source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 1–5, especially the local-determination and stabilization discussion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper develops stabilization-based Gaussian limits for local random geometric measures and random-graph functionals.
The paper studies treatment-effect asymptotics under a graphon-random exposure graph, proving direct-effect asymptotics and a consistent indirect-effect estimator.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Introduction, especially pp. 1–2 and Theorem 4 discussion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The preprint studies regression-adjusted ATE inference under graphon interference and gives a consistent asymptotic-variance estimator under a low-rank graphon model.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Resolve the minimax question with an explicit Le Cam family and a competing higher-order statistic, thereby determining whether the root-n separation rate is sharp at the coboundary boundary.

Add a power or sample-size comparison against the one-wave network-HAC workflow in Leung2022ANI for a concrete local-network subclass, making the practical value of the second wave quantitatively explicit.
State a short corollary identifying settings in which the two-wave statistic estimates a scientifically interpretable between-environment variation functional beyond the zero-boundary test.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0, retaining the two-wave/no-carryover design limitation explicitly and prioritizing the minimax-rate route.
